ex: In: a thing has something around it. The bear is in the box.

o: The teddy bear is in the box.
The teddy bear is behind the box.
The teddy bear is next to the box.
ex: The box is around the bear, so the bear is in the box.

p: Which word means almost the same as "in"?
ex: In and inside almost mean the same: the fish is in the bowl, inside the bowl.
On means touching the top. The apple touches the book, so it is on the book.
The apple is on the book, so the book is under the apple.

p: The apple touches the book. The apple is ___ the book.
ex: On = touching. Above = higher, not touching. The apple touches the book: on.
Under means lower, with something on top of it. The ball is under the table.
The ball is under the table, so the table is above the ball.
Behind: the tree hides part of the boy. The boy is behind the tree.
The boy is behind the tree, so the tree is in front of the boy.

o: The boy is behind the tree.
The boy is in front of the tree.
The boy is in the tree.
ex: The tree is closer to us and hides the boy: he is behind it.
In front of: nothing hides the dog. The dog is in front of the chair.
The dog is in front of the chair, so the chair is behind the dog.

o: The dog is in front of the chair.
The dog is under the chair.
The dog is behind the chair.
ex: The dog is closer to us than the chair: it is in front of the chair.
Behind and in front of are opposites. In and inside almost mean the same.
Between means in the middle of two things. The bear is between the plants.

o: The teddy bear is between the two plants.
The teddy bear is under the two plants.
The teddy bear is far from the two plants.
ex: There is a plant on each side of the bear: it is between them.

p: We say "between" when a thing is in the middle of…
ex: Between needs two things, one on each side: the bear is between two plants.
Next to means right at the side. The clock is next to the lamp.

o: The lamp is next to the clock.
The lamp is under the clock.
The lamp is far from the clock.
ex: They are side by side, so the lamp is next to the clock too.

p: Which two words can finish the sentence? "The clock is ___ the lamp."
ex: The clock is at the lamp's side and close to it: next to and near.
Near means close. The tree is close to the house: near the house.
The tree is near the house, so the house is near the tree too.
Far from means not close. The long arrow shows the tree is far from the house.
There is a long way between them, so the house is far from the tree.

p: Which one is the opposite of "near"?
ex: Near means close. Far from means not close. They are opposites.

p: Which two words tell that a thing is close?
ex: Near and next to are close. Far from is not close.
Above means higher, not touching. The lamp does not touch the table: above.
The lamp is above the table, so the table is below the lamp.

p: The lamp is higher than the table and does not touch it. The lamp is ___ the table.
ex: Above = higher, not touching. On = touching. The lamp does not touch: above.
Below means lower. The cat is lower than the shelf: below the shelf.
The books touch the top of the shelf, so they are on the shelf.

p: Which two words can finish the sentence? "The cat is ___ the shelf."
ex: Under and below both tell lower. The cat is under and below the shelf.
The books and the plant are on the shelf. The cat is below it.
Inside: the bowl is all around the fish. The fish is inside the bowl.

o: The fish is inside the bowl.
The fish is next to the bowl.
The fish is behind the bowl.
ex: The fish swims in the water of the bowl: it is inside the bowl.

p: Which two words can finish the sentence? "The fish is ___ the bowl."
ex: In and inside almost mean the same: the fish is in and inside the bowl.

p: Look at the window. The bird is flying ___ the trees.
ex: Over means up in the air, higher than something. The bird flies over the trees.

p: A bird stands on a branch and touches it. The bird is ___ the branch.
ex: On = touching. Over = up in the air, not touching. The bird touches: on.

p: Which two words tell that a thing is higher and NOT touching?
ex: Above and over do not touch. On touches.

p: Look at the table. Where is the pizza?
ex: The box is open and the pizza is in it: in the box.

p: There is a guitar ___ the lamp and the plant.
ex: The lamp is on one side, the plant on the other: between.
The dogs are under the table, below the top, between its legs.
The sofa hides part of the window, so the window is behind the sofa.
They are side by side, so the racket is next to the bag.
The cheese touches the plate, so it is on the plate.
The rug is closer to us than the sofa: it is in front of the sofa.
The lamp is lower than the shelf: it is under the shelf.
There are books on each side of the trophy: it is between the books.
On also means touching a wall. The picture is on the wall.

p: The two fish are ___ the bowl.
ex: The water and the bowl are around the fish: they are in the bowl.
